title: Did Armstrong's chops ever come back after 1934?
summary: DeMichael hears less brilliance in the 1935 Russell records; Randolph saw Armstrong still picking at his lip with a mirror and agrees.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You were talking earlier about Louis having chop trouble when he came back here in '34.
And I was listening to the records he made with Louis Russell's band in '35. And there's a distinct difference in his playing from the '33 band, the last records he made, --
-- and '35. The brilliance of tone seems to be gone. None of that wild, wonderful endings that he (unintelligible) Still superb, I'm not saying --
Did his chops ever come all the way back? Do you think?
I don't know whether they did or not.
Because I know -- I used to see him all the time, he'd carry a little mirror, and I used to see him all the time with that little mirror, looking at the -- and picking at his --
Yeah, I've seen him do that.
Yeah. And that would tell me right there that he still was having trouble with his chops.
But you've heard those records, I'm sure, from '35. Did you have that same feeling that it's not quite as brilliant as it was earlier.

Yeah, no, it wasn't. I listened to him quite a bit. I don't know, maybe someone would say, (unintelligible) well, you're just jealous because you're not there with him. It wasn't that, it's not that. I'll tell you one that, that man's really comical to work with, though.
